data.one_liner: Immutable collections based on SDK collections with builder pattern.
data.what_it_does: Provides immutable collection classes (like BuiltList, BuiltMap, BuiltSet) and corresponding mutable builder classes. Uses copy-on-write to avoid unnecessary copying and supports deep comparison and hashing.
use_when: You need safe, immutable collections to share across your app without defensive copying.
You want deep comparison and hashing support for collections.
You use built_value and need matching immutable collections.
avoid_when: You need direct mutability on standard SDK collection interfaces (built collections do not implement standard List/Set interfaces).
You want a fully codegen-free state model where native collections or other packages suffice.
strengths: Enforces immutability and prevents accidental state mutations.
Provides deep equality and caching for efficient comparisons and hashing.
Uses copy-on-write wrappers to avoid unnecessary data copying.
weaknesses: Collections do not implement core SDK mutable interfaces (e.g., BuiltList does not implement List).
Requires converting to/from builders or views when interoperating with standard SDK code.
